questions.stem: What does CLZ-200 add to the CLZ-190 VM pattern to install IIS without an interactive RDP session?

options.A: An Azure DNS A record
options.B: A Load Balancer outbound rule
options.C: Azure Custom Script Extension
options.D: A Terraform output block alone

optionExplanations.A: A DNS record names an address; it does not install software.
optionExplanations.B: Outbound rules translate network traffic rather than configure Windows features.
optionExplanations.C: The extension executes the lesson's PowerShell bootstrap inside the VM.
optionExplanations.D: Outputs expose values; they do not run guest installation commands.

questions.stem: Which publisher and extension type match the IIS resource in compute-windows.tf?

options.A: Microsoft.Compute and CustomScriptExtension
options.B: Microsoft.Azure.Extensions and CustomScript
options.C: Microsoft.Network and NetworkSecurityGroup
options.D: Microsoft.Storage and StorageAccount

optionExplanations.A: This is the Windows handler selected by the Terraform resource.
optionExplanations.B: That publisher/type combination is associated with the Linux handler.
optionExplanations.C: A network security group is not a guest script handler.
optionExplanations.D: Storage accounts cannot execute this Windows bootstrap handler.

questions.stem: Which PowerShell command installs the web-server role used by the bootstrap?

options.A: Set-Content -Name Web-Server
options.B: Resolve-DnsName -Name Web-Server
options.C: Get-Service -Name W3SVC
options.D: Install-WindowsFeature -Name Web-Server -IncludeManagementTools

optionExplanations.A: Set-Content writes file content, not Windows feature installations.
optionExplanations.B: DNS resolution does not install a Windows server role.
optionExplanations.C: Get-Service inspects service state without installing the feature.
optionExplanations.D: This installs IIS and the management tools on Windows Server.

questions.stem: Why does the script write index.html under C:\inetpub\wwwroot?

options.A: It stores Terraform's Azure resource IDs
options.B: It places the lesson page in IIS's default web root
options.C: It changes the VM's private IP allocation
options.D: It creates the administrator password

optionExplanations.A: Terraform resource bindings belong in state, not the IIS web root.
optionExplanations.B: IIS can serve this file through its default website.
optionExplanations.C: Guest HTML content cannot configure an Azure NIC address.
optionExplanations.D: The credential is generated by random_password, independently of this page.

questions.stem: A bootstrap may be triggered twice during troubleshooting. Which behavior best supports repeatability?

options.A: Installing the required feature and replacing the intended page with known content
options.B: Appending a new administrator account on every run
options.C: Deleting all websites before every command
options.D: Waiting for a user to confirm a console prompt

optionExplanations.A: The same desired guest configuration can be established repeatedly.
optionExplanations.B: Repeated runs would create unmanaged or duplicate identities.
optionExplanations.C: Broad destructive operations risk unrelated content and configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Extensions run unattended and cannot reliably answer interactive prompts.

questions.stem: Why is jsonencode used around the commandToExecute settings object?

options.A: It encrypts the Windows administrator password
options.B: It guarantees that IIS is healthy
options.C: It converts Terraform values into valid JSON for the extension
options.D: It removes the extension from state

optionExplanations.A: JSON encoding provides serialization rather than secret encryption.
optionExplanations.B: Correct JSON does not prove the command or service succeeded.
optionExplanations.C: The extension settings API expects JSON with correctly encoded strings.
optionExplanations.D: Serialization does not alter Terraform's resource ownership records.

questions.stem: The extension references azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.web.id. What relationship does that expression establish?

options.A: The VM depends on an HTTP response from the learner
options.B: The extension depends on the VM resource
options.C: The extension must run before the VM is created
options.D: The extension is deployed into every VM in the subscription

optionExplanations.A: The expression references the VM ID, not a network validation response.
optionExplanations.B: Terraform can infer that the VM must exist before attaching its extension.
optionExplanations.C: A VM extension needs its parent VM to exist.
optionExplanations.D: The reference identifies one specific Terraform-managed VM.

questions.stem: A script succeeds in an administrator's interactive session but uses that user's profile files. Why may it fail as an extension?

options.A: The extension always runs as the Terraform CLI user
options.B: The extension runs in the browser's JavaScript sandbox
options.C: The extension can execute only anonymous HTTP requests
options.D: Custom Script Extension runs as LocalSystem rather than that user's session

optionExplanations.A: The Azure guest execution identity is separate from the local CLI user.
optionExplanations.B: The bootstrap executes inside Windows, not the learner's browser.
optionExplanations.C: It runs guest commands, which can perform much more than web requests.
optionExplanations.D: User-specific paths and credentials may be unavailable to the extension.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid unsafe restarts during extension execution
questions.stem: An IIS bootstrap needs a reboot for an additional component. What is the safer extension design?

options.A: Restart the Azure VM Agent as the final command
options.B: Separate or schedule the reboot instead of restarting inside the running script
options.C: Loop on Restart-Computer until IIS returns 200
options.D: Ignore the reboot and claim full component readiness

optionExplanations.A: Stopping or updating the agent can leave extension operations incomplete.
optionExplanations.B: Restarting during extension execution can interrupt its completion.
optionExplanations.C: Repeated restarts prevent stable script completion and reliable validation.
optionExplanations.D: Readiness must be verified; a pending reboot cannot be assumed harmless.

questions.stem: A Custom Script Extension script runs longer than 90 minutes. What should the learner expect?

options.A: Azure automatically converts it into an Azure Automation runbook
options.B: Terraform silently raises the timeout to one day
options.C: The script is guaranteed to finish whenever the VM is stopped
options.D: The extension can fail provisioning because its runtime limit is exceeded

optionExplanations.A: The extension does not migrate long-running work to another service.
optionExplanations.B: Changing Terraform's wait behavior does not remove the handler's runtime limit.
optionExplanations.C: Stopping the VM interrupts execution rather than extending its runtime safely.
optionExplanations.D: Long bootstrap tasks need a different or shorter execution design.

questions.stem: Which proposed bootstrap change is most likely to stall unattended execution?

options.A: Using a predetermined lesson page string
options.B: Installing the Web-Server feature by name
options.C: Prompting the user to select a website name with Read-Host
options.D: Writing status information to a log file

optionExplanations.A: A known string can be written without user interaction.
optionExplanations.B: An explicit feature name supports unattended execution.
optionExplanations.C: There is no interactive learner console inside the extension run.
optionExplanations.D: Logging helps diagnosis without requiring an interactive response.

questions.stem: Azure reports the IIS extension as Transitioning immediately after apply. What is the best first response?

options.A: Inspect extension status and allow feature installation time before retrying
options.B: Open RDP from 0.0.0.0/0 to accelerate installation
options.C: Delete the resource group before checking any status
options.D: Declare the page ready because the VM exists

optionExplanations.A: Windows feature installation may still be running normally.
optionExplanations.B: Broadening network access neither speeds feature installation nor protects the VM.
optionExplanations.C: Premature deletion loses evidence and interrupts normal provisioning.
optionExplanations.D: A provisioned VM does not prove its guest bootstrap has completed.

questions.learningObjective: Validate application identity as well as connectivity
questions.stem: Which observation most strongly matches CLZ-200's expected web result?

options.A: A public IP appears in terraform output
options.B: The RDP port accepts a TCP connection
options.C: terraform fmt -check exits successfully
options.D: HTTP 200 plus content identifying the CLZ-200 lesson

optionExplanations.A: An allocated address does not show IIS is listening or serving content.
optionExplanations.B: Management connectivity does not validate the HTTP application.
optionExplanations.C: Formatting validates source layout rather than runtime application behavior.
optionExplanations.D: The response confirms both successful HTTP service and the intended page.

questions.stem: A browser displays the generic IIS welcome page with status 200. What remains unproven?

options.A: Whether HTTP is supported by Windows Server
options.B: Whether the public address exists
options.C: Whether the lesson's deterministic page was deployed
options.D: Whether Terraform uses an Azure provider

optionExplanations.A: The response already proves that an HTTP server replied.
optionExplanations.B: The successful request already used a reachable address.
optionExplanations.C: Status 200 alone cannot distinguish the desired page from default content.
optionExplanations.D: The HTTP body says nothing about the provider, and this is not the intended assertion.

questions.stem: After editing only an external script file, the page remains unchanged and the extension settings are identical. What should be reviewed?

options.A: A deliberate configuration or version change that triggers extension rerun
options.B: The Terraform output description text
options.C: A larger VNet address range
options.D: A new DNS TTL for the existing public IP

optionExplanations.A: Identical extension settings can prevent another execution of the script.
optionExplanations.B: Changing a description does not change guest execution settings.
optionExplanations.C: Address-space size does not trigger the IIS script to rerun.
optionExplanations.D: DNS caching does not explain unchanged guest content when execution was not retriggered.

questions.stem: A future bootstrap needs a short-lived artifact credential. Where should the extension configuration place sensitive parameters?

options.A: Public settings because jsonencode encrypts strings
options.B: Protected settings with an approved secret retrieval design
options.C: The HTML validation page
options.D: A committed terraform.tfvars.example containing the real credential

optionExplanations.A: Public JSON settings do not encrypt their contents.
optionExplanations.B: Protected settings are encrypted for the target VM; secret handling still needs care.
optionExplanations.C: Serving credentials as website content exposes them to visitors.
optionExplanations.D: Example files must not contain live credentials.

questions.stem: IIS is running but the public HTTP request times out. Which NSG destination port is relevant to this lesson's web test?

options.A: TCP 3389
options.B: TCP 53
options.C: TCP 80

optionExplanations.A: That port is used for RDP management rather than the HTTP page.
optionExplanations.B: DNS commonly uses port 53, not the lesson's web service.
optionExplanations.C: The output uses an http URL and the lesson permits TCP port 80.
optionExplanations.D: That frontend port belongs to the later RDP NAT lesson.

questions.stem: What is the intended value of admin_cidr for direct management in CLZ-200?

options.A: The entire Internet expressed as 0.0.0.0/0
options.B: The administrator's current public IPv4 address with a /32 prefix
options.C: The VM's own private IP with a /32 prefix
options.D: A public DNS hostname without a prefix

optionExplanations.A: That would broaden management exposure beyond the lesson's safety intent.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson limits RDP to one source address.
optionExplanations.C: The rule needs the external administrator source, not the destination VM address.
optionExplanations.D: The input expects an IPv4 CIDR rather than a hostname.

questions.stem: The allow-admin-rdp rule has priority 110 and deny-other-rdp has priority 120. Why can the selected administrator still connect?

options.A: Deny rules are ignored whenever a VM has a public IP
options.B: The rule with the larger number always wins
options.C: RDP traffic bypasses every Azure NSG
options.D: The matching allow rule is evaluated before the broader deny rule

optionExplanations.A: Public addresses do not disable NSG filtering.
optionExplanations.B: NSG processing uses ascending numeric priority.
optionExplanations.C: RDP is subject to normal NSG traffic evaluation.
optionExplanations.D: Lower NSG priority numbers are evaluated first.

questions.stem: What does terraform output -raw iis_url supply for the validation script?

options.A: The VM public IP formatted as an HTTP URL
options.B: An automatically trusted HTTPS certificate
options.C: The extension's detailed execution log
options.D: The administrator password followed by the hostname

optionExplanations.A: The output is constructed from the Standard public IP address.
optionExplanations.B: The introductory configuration does not create TLS certificate infrastructure.
optionExplanations.C: Extension logs and provisioning state require separate inspection.
optionExplanations.D: The password is exposed through a separate sensitive output.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish network allocation from service readiness
questions.stem: Why can a Standard static public IP exist before the web page is usable?

options.A: Network provisioning and guest IIS installation complete at different stages
options.B: Static means the address cannot carry HTTP traffic
options.C: The public IP resource installs IIS only during destroy
options.D: Terraform outputs always refer to an older subscription

optionExplanations.A: An address allocation does not establish guest service readiness.
optionExplanations.B: Static allocation concerns address assignment rather than supported application protocol.
optionExplanations.C: The extension installs IIS during deployment, not cleanup.
optionExplanations.D: Outputs come from the selected state and are not inherently stale across subscriptions.

questions.stem: Which production change addresses this lesson's intentional direct web-VM exposure?

options.A: Allow every TCP port because the page is public
options.B: Use the generated password as an HTTP query parameter
options.C: Keep HTTP-only access and disable all health checks
options.D: Place IIS behind an approved delivery tier and use private management

optionExplanations.A: Broad access creates unnecessary exposure rather than a production design.
optionExplanations.B: Credentials in URLs can leak through logs and browser history.
optionExplanations.C: Production guidance calls for TLS, health checks, and operational controls.
optionExplanations.D: The production guidance replaces direct VM access with controlled ingress and administration.

questions.stem: Where can detailed Custom Script Extension logs be found inside Windows?

options.A: Only in the local terraform.tfvars file
options.B: Under C:\WindowsAzure\Logs\Plugins\Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension
options.C: Inside the Azure public IP resource's tags
options.D: In the browser's local progress storage

optionExplanations.A: Variable files are inputs and do not contain guest execution logs.
optionExplanations.B: The handler writes diagnostic logs under its WindowsAzure plugin path.
optionExplanations.C: Tags hold metadata rather than extension script logs.
optionExplanations.D: Learning progress cannot collect guest system logs by itself.

questions.stem: The input still contains 203.0.113.10/32. What must happen before expecting direct RDP from the learner's workstation?

options.A: Use that value because every home router translates to it
options.B: Change it to the VM's generated public IP
options.C: Replace it with the learner's actual current public IPv4 /32
options.D: Remove /32 and use the same bare value

optionExplanations.A: Documentation addresses do not represent all Internet clients.
optionExplanations.B: The rule matches the administrator source, not the destination public IP.
optionExplanations.C: The documentation-range placeholder is not the learner's live source address.
optionExplanations.D: The input requires a CIDR and a correctly scoped source.

questions.stem: Why is the Windows Server 2022 image reference not sufficient evidence that IIS is installed?

options.A: Every Azure Windows image permanently includes the lesson page
options.B: The extension separately installs Web-Server after the VM is provisioned
options.C: Changing an Azure tag installs the required role
options.D: The public IP performs the feature installation

optionExplanations.A: A base image cannot contain this deployment-specific page automatically.
optionExplanations.B: The selected base image and the lesson's application configuration are separate concerns.
optionExplanations.C: Tags describe resources; they do not configure Windows roles.
optionExplanations.D: The network address resource does not execute guest commands.

questions.stem: The generated administrator password output is sensitive. What protection is still necessary?

options.A: Protect Terraform state and any explicit password output files
options.B: Commit state because sensitive outputs are omitted from it
options.C: Send the state file to anyone who can view the lesson page
options.D: Remove the password output and assume the state has no password

optionExplanations.A: Sensitive marking hides routine display but does not remove the value from state.
optionExplanations.B: Traditional sensitive values can remain in state.
optionExplanations.C: Website visibility does not authorize access to administrator credentials.
optionExplanations.D: Removing an output does not remove the VM credential stored by resources.

questions.stem: Why does the deploy sequence run terraform show tfplan before terraform apply tfplan?

options.A: To start IIS while leaving Azure resources undeployed
options.B: To publish Terraform state as a website
options.C: To inspect the saved changes that will be applied
options.D: To guarantee that every HTTP request will succeed

optionExplanations.A: Showing a plan is read-only and does not run a guest script.
optionExplanations.B: The show command does not deploy documentation or state websites.
optionExplanations.C: The learner reviews the same saved plan later passed to apply.
optionExplanations.D: A reviewed plan cannot guarantee runtime health or network reachability.

questions.stem: The page is no longer needed but the Windows VM remains allocated. Which action best ends this lesson's managed resource footprint?

options.A: Close the browser tab showing the IIS page
options.B: Run terraform fmt repeatedly until no differences remain
options.C: Delete only index.html from the guest
options.D: Run the documented Terraform destroy and verify the resource group is absent

optionExplanations.A: Closing a browser does not change Azure infrastructure or billing.
optionExplanations.B: Source formatting cannot remove billable cloud resources.
optionExplanations.C: Deleting application content leaves the underlying infrastructure deployed.
optionExplanations.D: Destroy removes the managed VM, disk, public IP, and network resources.

sources.title: Azure virtual machine states and billing

questions.stem: Why capture resource_group_name before destroying CLZ-200?

options.A: To retain the group name for the post-destroy Azure existence check
options.B: To prevent Terraform from deleting its managed VM
options.C: To make the public IP permanently free
options.D: To export the administrator password to GitHub

optionExplanations.A: Terraform outputs may no longer be available once their resources are removed.
optionExplanations.B: Capturing an output does not change the destroy plan.
optionExplanations.C: Saving a resource name cannot alter Azure billing.
optionExplanations.D: The captured value is the group name, and secrets should not be published.

questions.stem: HTTP times out and the extension is Failed. Which next step is most useful before changing network rules?

options.A: Replace the NSG with an allow-all rule immediately
options.B: Inspect the extension's error and script logs
options.C: Increase instance_count in this single-VM lesson
options.D: Mark the exercise complete because Terraform has a state file

optionExplanations.A: That broadens access without addressing the extension failure.
optionExplanations.B: A failed guest bootstrap can explain an absent IIS service.
optionExplanations.C: More infrastructure does not fix the recorded script error.
optionExplanations.D: State existence does not establish successful runtime configuration.
